summary: The report's cited figures and finding summaries check out. Two required details are missing: per-row K mutation status and an explanation or explicit unknown for the CI time increase.
blocking_findings: F27 [Blocker] review-a: report.md:81–161 lists the 77 K groups, but it does not mark each row as lacking a mutation check. The single summary sentence at line 161 does not provide per-row status. spec.md:35 requires each K row without a mutation check to list that status. Add the status to every row or enumerate every affected row.

F28 [Blocker] review-a: report.md:244–248 reports the 7.64-second increase and timing components, but it does not state a reason for the increase or say that the cause is not recorded. Add one evidence-based explanation or state that the cause is unknown.
evidence: git rev-parse HEAD returned 4d41866fdde7d7c53359684485682e6fd06b27a5, matching role_base_sha and audited_head_sha.

The report's baseline figures match baseline.json and baseline.log: 3175 cases, 86.52% line coverage, and 90.47 seconds. Its final figures match gate-66aeb1011.json and green-66aeb1011.log: 1412 cases, 92.07% line coverage, and 98.11 seconds.
The merge figures match gate-257a6b0c.json: 3094 to 1385 cases, 1709 removed, and the blog validation reduced from 1726 cases to 17.
The reported pre-merge comparison is consistent: Phase 2 ended at 3094; the final count without the 1709-case merge would be 3121. That is a 54-case or 1.7% cut from 3175.
All 10 commit SHAs in the per-class table resolve with git cat-file -e. The plan task lines match the listed D1-D5, R2, and blog-merge SHAs and case counts.
The K table contains 77 groups and sums to 2843 cases, matching classification.md:226. The seven tutor-commission file paths have an empty diff from a1caa5803 to HEAD.
The K section does not report mutation-check status on any row. Report.md:161 says only, 'No K row carries a mutation check.' This does not meet the per-row reporting requirement in spec.md:35.
Report.md:246–248 states the duration increased by 7.64 seconds and gives component timings. It neither attributes the increase nor says that the cause is not recorded.
The report states that the 20% target is met through the blog merge, names the 1709-case merge, and acknowledges the result without that merge would be only a 1.7% cut.
The findings section includes F1-F26 and ADV-1–ADV-24 once each, with an escape description, finding role, and fix or note. Six spot checks against review and acceptance JSONs match.
Spot checks confirm F17 remains an open nit, F18 retains default A pending PM confirmation, F25 is closed, F26 remains a portability note, ADV-8 is closed, and ADV-23 remains a note.
The report includes the lessons and open PM items. Its prose is clear overall; long sentences do not hide another factual discrepancy.
The plan records Phase 4 tasks 4.1–4.3 complete and cites the report, commit, gate, and timing logs.
